criteria.criterion: docs/spec.toml OLY-9-09 has mechanism naming the new crates/athena-core module and its function (not "none"), owner "Athena", and a measure ending in `status: repeated`.
criteria.evidence: I read the diff of docs/spec.toml. The mechanism is "crates/athena-core/src/learning.rs (join, run by crates/athena-core/src/status.rs and printed by crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs)", the owner is "Athena", and the measure ends with "; status: repeated". `learning::join` exists in the new file.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core learning`: a fixture with a repeated failure class, a landed addressing request, and a specialization/class-trend outcome yields one line per class that names the class, the request and its landed/open state, and the outcome. The same test fails if the join function is stubbed to return nothing.
criteria.evidence: 2 tests passed. `learning_joins_a_class_to_its_landed_request_and_the_outcome` gives join two causes in class FC-1, one in FC-2 and one with no class. It asserts exactly 2 lines, each matching its full expected string: FC-1 with request job-9 (landed), "specialization helps: big · high" and "trend: improving"; FC-2 with job-8 (open). A stub that returns an empty Vec would fail the `lines.len() == 2` check and the line checks. I did not run a stubbed build; this follows from reading the assertions.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-cli`: the status display prints the new lines under the `repeated` label, and prints nothing extra when there are no repeated causes (an empty history is not shown as success).
criteria.evidence: The display test `repeated_causes_are_listed_with_their_counts_and_the_request_that_addresses_them` passed. It asserts `learning_section(&[], true) == ""`. With a line, it asserts the output is "repeated    learning: ..." when the label is free, and an unlabelled continuation line otherwise. In `status()`, the learning section is pushed right after the repeated-causes section (display.rs:1346). The full athena-cli suite passed in Athena's recorded `cargo test --locked`. The test covers `learning_section` only, not the whole `status()` output; see findings.

findings.summary: The learning join includes causes that the repeated section excludes: dormant causes and closed (landed) causes.
findings.evidence: `join` gets `all_causes` before the `is_open` filter and before dormant causes are split out. A class whose stage athena.toml switched off can therefore get a `learning:` line under `repeated` and also appear in the dormant section. Showing landed causes is intended (it shows the improvement's outcome), but the dormant overlap is not documented.

findings.summary: Specialization and class trend are now computed twice per status call.
findings.evidence: `specialization(&records)` and `ClassTrend::compute(&records)` run once for `learning` and again at lines 1269/1278 for the StatusView fields. Computing each once and reusing it would be simpler.

findings.summary: No test covers the end-to-end wiring from Records::status through display::status.
findings.evidence: The CLI test exercises `learning_section` directly. Nothing asserts that `status(&StatusView)` places learning lines after the repeated causes, or that `Records::status` fills `learning`. The wiring is a single line on each side.

findings.summary: The outcome is attributed to the request's class of work, not to the failure class.
findings.evidence: Role effectiveness is approximated by the specialization verdict and trend of the addressing job's class of work. The reading accepted this approach. It is a proxy, not a measured before/after on the failure class itself.

summary: The change passes. It adds `athena_core::learning::join`, which takes each repeated failure class and links it to the request that addresses it (landed or open) and to how that request's class of work is doing: the specialization verdict and the minutes trend. `athena status` prints these lines under the `repeated` label and prints nothing when no cause repeated. docs/spec.toml now records OLY-9-09's mechanism, owner Athena, and a measure ending in `status: repeated`. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core learning` and `cargo test -p athena-cli repeated_causes`; both passed. The core test checks the exact joined lines, so a stubbed join would fail it. fmt, clippy and the full test suite passed in Athena's recorded CI run. Every changed file is on the expected-deliverables list. There are three minor findings, none blocking: the join also covers dormant and closed causes, so a dormant cause can appear twice in the output; specialization and trend are computed twice per status call; and no test covers the full status rendering. The snapshot status view prints only counts and throughput, so I could not see the new lines on real records.
